title: Good And Evil | Generation To Generation: From Beginning To End

sense.text: The class is the battle of good versus evil, from the beginning of time to the end of time, and it starts here. “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”: our image is the Father, the Son and the angels. Make man in our image.

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.” Genesis 2 elaborates on chapter 1: it gives more emphasis on how man was made, and on when the female was made.

“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground”: Adam was a black man. He formed Adam from the dust of the ground; he formed a black man. “And breathed into his nostrils the breath of life”: spirit was placed inside of him, “and man became a living soul.”
“And the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.” He put the man in the garden eastward in Eden.

A river went out of Eden and “became into four heads.” Pison is the Nile River, the White Nile, and Havilah is Saudi Arabia: write that down. Gihon is the Blue Nile, “the same is it that compasseth the whole land of Ethiopia.” Hiddekel is the Tigris River, “which goeth toward the east of Assyria.” “And the fourth river is Euphrates”: that’s self-explanatory, the Euphrates River.

So that’s where the garden is, where it was in the beginning: in that land mass, that region. It was massive, and Adam was placed eastward within it.

“And the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.” He formed Adam from the dust outside the garden and placed Adam inside the garden. He gave him a job: he made him a husbandman.

“Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it”: thou shalt not learn of it or eat of it, partake in it. “For in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.” Adam knew good; he did not know good and evil.

“It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” Genesis 1 says male and female created he them; this gives emphasis on when the female was made. Adam was alone at this time. God formed him, placed him in the garden, made him a husbandman and gave him a job; now he’s going to give him a woman.

Adam named the creatures God had formed: that was another job he had. All the beasts of the field and fowls had mates, but “for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.” Adam was alone while he was doing this, and Adam had the wisdom and understanding to name the animals.

God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, took one of his ribs and “made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” He formed the rib out of Adam, turned it into a woman and brought her to Adam. This is a marriage here.
“She shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” He named the beasts of the field, the fish of the sea and the fowls of heaven, and he named her woman, for she came out of him.

“And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.” They were both naked and not ashamed means they were innocent: they did not learn evil yet. To sum it up, they were naked and not ashamed.

“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field”: this serpent was most subtle, and the class goes to see what it was. “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” He’s questioning her: God tell you that?

That is twofold. One, he’s the devil, so he’s wiser than everybody there; but it also goes into something more regarding the beasts of the field.
“God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.” The tree in the midst of the garden is good and evil. Who taught her that? Adam taught her that.
“Ye shall not surely die”: meaning not immediately. He’s playing games with her, semantics.

Then he gives her a reason why God told her not to eat of the tree, like a heads up: this is the reason why God said you can’t do it. “Your eyes shall be opened”: you’ll gain wisdom beyond your understanding, you’ll be enlightened. I’m going to tell you what God don’t want you to know.

“And ye shall be as gods”: not only will your husband be a god, you’ll be a god too, just like your man. You’ll be equal. Ain’t that what you always wanted, Eve? Because that’s what she wanted. “Knowing good and evil”: you’ll know both good and evil. Good and evil goes right back to that tree God said don’t eat from, and the one who introduced it was the devil.

“The tree was good for food”: good to take in, to learn, to apply. “Pleasant to the eyes”: she liked what she saw. “A tree to be desired to make one wise”: to make her wise, to learn what good and evil is. She took of it and did eat, and she brought it to Adam too, “and he did eat.”

The Bible is an abbreviation. It’s not like Eve came to Adam one day and said, let’s be idolaters. It was gradual: hey, I learned something. It took time; it wasn’t immediate.

“And the eyes of them both were opened”: both of them gained the enlightenment of what good is and what evil is. “And they knew that they were naked”: they realized, by us doing this we’re sinful, this is wrong. They learned at that moment that they messed up. Earlier it said they were naked and not ashamed; here they knew they were naked, meaning they knew they were sinful.

“They sewed fig leaves together”: they started to hide the evidence. Let’s hide this stuff, God’s going to find out what we did.
Adam and his wife hid themselves “amongst the trees of the garden”: amongst the people.

“I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.” “Who told thee that thou wast naked?” Where’d you learn that from? How do you know you’re naked? That means you did something I told you not to do.

“The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree”: she did it, it’s her fault. He blamed God too: you gave me that woman and she made me mess up. All the accountability is removed from him.
“What is this that thou hast done?” What you do, Eve? “The serpent beguiled me”: the devil did it, he made me do it. Everyone’s pointing fingers at each other.

Go slow here, because this is the premise of the whole class. The Lord said to the devil, “Because thou hast done this”, because you have done this, Satan, “thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”: you’ll be cursed above all the other beasts of the field.

“Upon thy belly shalt thou go”: meaning on the ground. I’m going to place you on earth; that’s your station, that will be your domain, your realm. That’s why it says dust and upon your belly: the dust is earth.

“And I will put enmity between thee and the woman”: hatred between you, Satan, and the woman Eve. “And between thy seed”: your seed, Satan, “and her seed”: her children.

“It shall bruise thy head”: it, Satan, shall bruise your head, talking to Eve now. “And thou shalt bruise his heel”: your seed shall bruise his heel. What’s your heel? Your heel is your bottom, your feet. That comes back later.

“Unto the woman he said”: talking to her now, Eve. “I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception”: sorrow is the menstruation you have every month, and conception is labor pains. “In sorrow thou shalt bring forth children”: labor pains.

“And thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Why is the Lord telling her this? Because her desire was to Satan, to learn from him. He said no, you learn from your husband; he rules over you, not the devil. Stay in your place. She stepped out of her place, and because she did that, Adam let her take him out of his place. It’s a domino effect: Satan said, I can’t get him, but I can get him through her.

So the first attack of Satan in the Bible is the attack on the black couple, the family, and it starts with the woman first. He’s doing the same in the black community today, using the woman: YouTube women, podcasts, women’s talk shows, women’s magazines, women in the music industry, women in the sex industry. Satan uses the woman.

“Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife”: because Adam listened to the woman. “And hast eaten of the tree”: you indulged in idolatry, that’s what he’s saying. “Cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life.” When Adam was in the garden he was a husbandman and it was light, it was easy, because it watered itself. Now God says, I’m going to kick you out of here, and the soil outside the garden you’re going to work your behind off. Now we call it nine to five, overtime, paid days off, PTO.

“In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground”: you’re going to work till you die. The retirement age was 63, now it’s 70, and if we’re here 20 or 30 more years it’ll be damn near 80. “For out of it wast thou taken”: out of the earth were you taken. “For dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return”: you shall die. Death was brought into the world because of this.

This proves they birthed nations and people and kindreds and tribes. She was called woman because she came out of man: in Genesis 2 he named what she was. Then he says, but your name is Eve, “because she was the mother of all living.” She was everyone’s mom on the earth; Adam and Eve parented everyone on the planet.

Eve means beginning, like New Year’s Eve: the eve of something is the beginning of something. All life came out of Eve.

Once Adam and Eve sinned, God gave them coats of skins, “and clothed them.” Once they sinned they knew good and evil, and knowing good and evil, something must happen: they had to sacrifice animals and do sin offerings. The sacrificial law was instituted. That’s the coats of skins that clothed them, covered their sins. Before, they were innocent, naked and not ashamed, not sinning; now they must clothe themselves with sacrifice. To clothe yourself means to atone.

Adam and Eve are still in the garden, and they know good and evil now. “Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever”: he can’t live forever being like that. He can’t know evil and be good and be immortal with us.

“Therefore the Lord God sent him forth from the garden of Eden”: Adam got an eviction notice. Adam and Eve got kicked out of the garden because of their sinful nature; they acknowledged it, learned of it. “To till the ground from whence he was taken”: he was formed from that ground and put in the garden, then kicked out and put right back where he was formed from.

The garden of Eden is paradise, the paradise Ezra says the Lord put him into. He was created here on the earth and then put in paradise, and he was kicked out of paradise to this earth where God created him. You can’t be there in the midst of sin.

He placed at the east of the garden of Eden “Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way”. Where the garden of Eden was, he placed these things at the east of it. A sword that turns every way, this way and that way, is not stable, not standing in one place: it causes confusion. No one can enter in, and it causes confusion so you don’t know where it is and can’t find a way back in again. “To keep the way of the tree of life”: to keep you out, so you cannot enter back in. Keep that flaming sword in mind.

precepts.why:
“As the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.” “For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or if ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received, or another gospel, which ye have not accepted, ye might well bear with him.”

Anyone that comes with a different doctrine, or spirit, or Christ, they all come from Satan. The same spirit that beguiled Eve in the garden is the same spirit that brings forth Christianity today. All these different doctrines and philosophies and religions are Satan based. Satan was the one that tricked Eve in Genesis 3.

What were they involved in, regarding them becoming naked and knowing that they were naked? “Then I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf.” Aaron made a golden calf, an idol for Israel to worship in Moses’ absence. Israel grew impatient at Moses’ disappearance and said, we want an idol to worship, so Aaron made an idol, a golden calf.

“And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:)” How? By getting them involved in idolatry. That’s the clue right there: Adam and Eve indulged in learning good and evil through idolatry. Idolatry was the nakedness. That’s why Adam said, I’m naked, and the Lord said, how do you know you’re naked? Because you went in there and learned evil, which is idolatry.

Death was brought into the world because of this. “O Lord, who bearest rule, thou spakest at the beginning, when thou didst plant the earth”, and gavest “a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands”, and didst “breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee.”

“And thou leadest him into paradise”: Adam was formed from the dust of the ground outside of paradise, then he was placed in paradise, “which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Before the earth, paradise was already in existence.

“And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed”: commandments were around back then. “And immediately thou appointedst death in him”: death was sown in Adam the moment he listened to his wife and indulged in idolatry. “And in his generations”: he eventually died, and that was passed into his generations; we all eventually die too.

“Of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” Adam and Eve parented nations of people, in the garden and outside the garden: millions of people. Adam and Eve had a whole bunch of babies. And because of Adam, every people walked after their own will: everyone became self-willed, doing what they wanted.

“Of the woman came the beginning of sin”: because Satan came to her first. “And through her we all die”: through Eve death was brought into the world, and Adam listened. Be mad if you want; that’s what it says. I don’t write this.

How was Satan able to convince Eve to eat of the tree she was told not to eat of? It’s very simple: “Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world”. Satan played on Eve’s envy, the desire to be equal. He couldn’t get Adam, because Adam already had the power she wanted. That’s why he said to her, ye shall be as gods: there was only one god in that house, and Eve wanted there to be two gods in the house. That’s what brought death into the world.

“And they that do hold of his side do find it”: they that hold to Satan’s side find death.

That’s why you have death in the black and brown community today too: Eve wants to be God too, Eve wants to be the head of the household too. Same scenario: the serpent played on Eve again. And there are levels to that death: when you don’t know your identity, you dead; when you don’t know where you come from, you dead; when you don’t know God’s laws, you dead.

Coats of skins to cover them, to clothe them. “And the bullock for the sin offering, and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall one carry forth without the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung.”

So what did Adam and Eve have to do? They had to sacrifice animals and do sin offerings. The sacrificial law was instituted, and that’s the coats of skins that clothed them, covered their sins.

This goes with Exodus 32:25, what the sin was. “For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication”. That’s why Aaron, when he made the golden calf, made Israel naked to their shame. Idolatry causes nakedness: not so much physical, but spiritual.

This sums it all up. “For the worshipping of idols not to be named”: not named here because it wasn’t named in Genesis, “is the beginning”, the Genesis, “the cause, and the end, of all evil.”

Idolatry was the sin Adam and Eve were involved in in the beginning. That’s the good and evil: there’s understanding in idolatry, but there’s evil in it too. God’s laws are good, righteousness; Satan introduces both. You can do good, but you can also do good in this evil way: it gives you a back door. Good and evil are always going to be together.

sense.text: “Son of man, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his multitude”: his army, his realm. “Whom art thou like in thy greatness?” Who do you resemble, Pharaoh, in your greatness, before you fall? This chapter is a parable, a comparison between Pharaoh in his greatness and someone else.

“Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with fair branches”: a cedar is a tree in Lebanon. He mentions the Assyrian because the Assyrians conquered Egypt; before Assyria came into power, Pharaoh, Egypt, was in its greatness. “His top was among the thick boughs”: powerful.
“The waters made him great”, and his height was exalted above all the trees of the field “because of the multitude of waters”. It’s talking about somebody else here, and it’s going to elaborate.
“Under his shadow dwelt all great nations.” Remember Ezra said that out of Adam came kindreds, people, tribes and nations.
“Thus was he fair in his greatness, in the length of his branches: for his root was by great waters”: meaning great wisdom came from him.

“The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him”: the cedars in the garden of God, in paradise, could not hide him, because he stood out from all the rest. He was the most glorified of them all. “Nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty”: because he was the wisest.

“All the trees of Eden, that were in the garden of God, envied him.” How can a tree envy? A tree is not a person. The tree is not a tree, it’s a person: people are trees, because trees are abundant and very tall, huge.

So it’s talking about Adam here. Adam is being compared to both Assyria and Pharaoh, because Assyria was a very ancient empire that reigned in the beginning, and Egypt was a very ancient empire that reigned in the beginning.

“Because thou hast lifted up thyself in height”: “I have therefore delivered him into the hand of the mighty one of the heathen”, Egypt falling into Assyria. “I have driven him out for his wickedness”: who was driven out for wickedness? Adam. It goes back and forth between them.

“And strangers, the terrible of the nations, have cut him off”: going into Assyria and Egypt. “His branches are fallen, and his boughs are broken”: when Adam fell, all the wisdom Adam taught the people began to diminish; it’s gone, Adam is gone. “And all the people of the earth are gone down from his shadow”: from Adam’s shadow. And they left him, “Upon his ruin”.

“To the end that none of all the trees by the waters exalt themselves for their height”: because their understanding starts to diminish, and they lose their stature over time. “For they are all delivered unto death”: when Adam died, Ezra says death was appointed in him and in his generations.

“To the nether parts of the earth”: nether means lower in position, lying beneath the earth’s surface, infernal, lower or under. Adam was in paradise before, and he was brought to the nether part: Adam got kicked out and he got put here. This is nether earth we’re in now. This is garbage, the bottom. That’s why he told Satan, you’re going to rule this. All the nations that are beneath us remain here. “In the midst of the children of men”: everybody else, “with them that go down to the pit”, with them that die.

“In the day when he went down to the grave”: when Adam died, “I caused a mourning”. Everyone cried: this dude died, and now we’re all going to die with him. We had paradise, now we’re going to be on earth. When Adam got kicked out, everyone got kicked out, the tribes, the nations, the people. God said, all of you get out, because you’re all like him. Now we can’t grow no more, we’re going to lose our stature, we’re getting dumber, because Adam is gone.

“I covered the deep for him”: all the deep understanding and wisdom they had through Adam, they’re losing it now he’s gone. “And all the trees of the field fainted for him”: trees don’t faint, people do. The trees fainted for Adam when he died, meaning his children.

“I made the nations to shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to hell with them that descend into the pit”. When Adam fell it was catastrophic. Whatever it was, they don’t say, but it was bad, very bad. “All the trees of Eden”, “all that drink water, shall be comforted in the nether parts of the earth”: comforted here.

“They also went down into hell with him”: everyone got kicked out, everyone is on nether earth now. “Unto them that be slain with the sword”: death was appointed in them too, like him. “They that were his arm, that dwelt under his shadow in the midst of the heathen”: his arm is his flesh, his descendants.

“To whom art thou thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden?” He asks the question again. Pharaoh, before Assyria conquered you, you were like Adam: boastful, people came under you for sanctuary, you had resources, wealth, power, everybody came to you to learn wisdom. Now where are you? Assyria came and destroyed you. Adam was like both of them in a certain way: like Assyria in his glory and like Pharaoh in glory, but both their falls were terrible and everybody felt it, the same way everyone felt it when Adam fell.

“Yet shalt thou be brought down with the trees of Eden unto the nether parts of the earth”, with everybody else. “This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, saith the Lord God”: but it’s not just Pharaoh, it’s who he’s compared to also. Pharaoh and Adam.

precepts.why:
“For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed”: the first Adam, because there were other Adams after him. “Bearing a wicked heart”: in Genesis 3 he didn’t know he was naked, or had a wicked heart, until they actually performed wickedness; then they realized at that moment that they were naked. He “was overcome”, by Eve, “and so be all they that are born of him”: they have a wicked heart and can be overcome.

“Thus infirmity was made permanent”: sin was made permanent through Adam. Out of Adam’s loins you are sinful. “And the law (also) in the heart of the people with the malignity of the root”: the law was put in us, but there was also the good and evil in us. You have the old man in you and the new man there, an ongoing battle in us from the moment we’re born. Adam learned good and evil, so anything that came out of him had good and evil inside of it. That’s the root.

Malignant means tending to produce death or deterioration: it corrupts over time. It’s cancerous, it’s bad. When Adam did what he did, his seed that came out of him was bound to deteriorate. Did he die immediately when he got kicked out? No. Satan told Eve, ye shall not surely die: not immediately, but over time you and your descendants will deteriorate.

“So that the good departed away”: the law in time was forgotten, because Adam died and the law was dismissed after a while, “and the evil abode still”: the evil spread.

“Unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him”. Remember Satan said, ye shall not surely die; this says that as soon as he went in with Eve, immediately. Death came to him immediately, but he died over time: deterioration, malignity. “And in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number”: out of Eve.

“And every people walked after their own will”: at the fall of Adam, “and did wonderful things before thee”, meaning evil stuff before God, “and despised thy commandments”, because the law was with us at first, but then the evil abode still and the law was forgotten.

“And again in process of time”: keep those three words in mind. Process of time means a while; it could be a hundred years later. “Thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them. And it came to pass in every of them, that as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.” When Adam died it was as catastrophic as the flood was. That’s why Ezekiel 31 says that at his fall the nations shook. It wasn’t, okay Adam, get out, time to go, and everyone just walked out. It was very, very bad.

All this had to happen to bring us to Christ. It was all predestined to happen: the Lord’s plan, his screenplay, and we’re all just actors in it. “For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly”: he didn’t want to be, “but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope”.

He made Adam sinful on purpose. He knew Adam would fall into that, so that it would bring sin into the world, so that Christ would come into the world and grant us repentance and grant us life. The Father knew this. That was God’s plan from the very beginning.

sense.text: “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment”: red in shade and hairy all over. “And they called his name Esau”: he lacked pigmentation.

“And his hand took hold on Esau’s heel”. Why does it emphasize this? This emphasizes the beginning of the so-called white man and the so-called Negro today, and the fight for power. Esau came out first, Jacob came out after and grabbed hold of that heel. They were fighting in the womb, and the fight continued outside the womb with him grabbing his heel.

Why isn’t Jacob described here? He looked normal. Esau did not look normal at all, and still don’t.
Keep this in mind: “And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.” Esau was a cunning hunter and a man of the field.

precepts.why: Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; this shows what Jacob was. He’s talking to his father-in-law Laban: “For it was little which thou hadst before I came, and it is now increased unto a multitude; and the Lord hath blessed thee since my coming”. “I will again feed and keep thy flock”, “removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the brown cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and of such shall be my hire.”

“So the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s. And the man increased exceedingly”: Jacob, “and had much cattle”.

So Jacob was a keeper of sheep and cattle, and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field. Esau was the man of the field, and Jacob was a man that dealt with the cattle.

sense.text: “And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.” Cain means a man.
“And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground”: a man of the field. Sound familiar? Esau was a man of the field and Jacob kept the cattle.
“And in process of time”: those three words again. It means this was gradual, not immediate; it took a while for this to happen.

The Lord had respect to Abel’s offering, but unto Cain’s offering “he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” “Why art thou wroth?” What’s wrong with you? “Why is thy countenance fallen?” What’s wrong with your face?

“If thou doest well”: if you righteously offer the sacrifices that I want, “shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well”: you offering fruit, I didn’t ask for no fruit. It says process of time: he knew to do better, but he got tired of doing it, because he was evil. “Sin lieth at the door”: Satan lies at the door of your mind, on your head, playing you for a fool.

Why would the Lord check him, if he only brought vegetables? Because he already knew the law of sacrifice, and he decided to bring in food, whatever he wanted to do. That’s the same thing the white man does today: he wants to worship the Lord the way he wants to, not the way of the laws and commandments the Lord set up.

“And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him”: you’re going to gain the power of the devil. He already was a devil.
“Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” This took time; it wasn’t immediate. He got fed up and eventually he killed Abel.

“I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?” He had a smart mouth on top of it: after he kills him he goes, am I his keeper, how am I supposed to know where he is? Talking to God like that: the boldness, the evil of this dude.
“What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground”: you killed him, and he’s talking to me.

“And now art thou cursed from the earth”: cursed means I’m going to take your pigmentation from you, I’m going to take your color from you. You’re made from the earth, but you ain’t going to look like it. “Which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand”: now you’re going to resemble the same color as your brother’s blood that you shed in the ground.

So when you look at Esau today, his blood shows through his flesh: he matches the blood of his brother that he shed, to this day. It goes back to the red pottage when he came back as Esau: he’s referred to as red because he’s a murderer, a bloody man. He looks according to what he is. Just look at his work in this earth, throughout Africa, throughout America: he loves blood. His name is called Edom, and Edom means more than red: it means bloody, because red is blood.

The Most High does everything for a reason. You can see the blood under his skin because he’s a murderer, a bloody man. That’s why he tries to hide by messing around with dark nations, but the Most High said nope, I’m still going to have you look the way you look. You can marry the darkest woman you can find, and that child comes out red, some real brown and some as red as blood itself, with black mamas. You can hide some of the time, but not all the time. Look at the news in Gaza: who’s doing all the killing? That man is a bloody dude; he could not help himself.

“When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength”: because your brother’s blood was spilled in it, I’m going to curse the land for you wherever you go. That’s why Europe is a freaking wasteland; they’ve got to import everything. If it were not for Africa, Europe would be a third world country. That’s a fact; it’s a bottomless pit over there. Wherever Esau goes the earth does not yield its strength. That’s why they go with GMOs: fake fruit, fake seeds, fake plants, fake meat, fake animals, polyester instead of linen and cotton, plastic, man-made material, not of God. The land here in the Americas was plenteous and prosperous and blessed with fruits; Esau came here, and now dying trees, garbage weather, sickness, disease, rats. Wherever he goes, death follows. And the nations are catching up with him: they know who he is.

“A fugitive”: you’re going to kill, murder and get away with it. On a higher scale: what they did to our brothers in Congo, the colonization and murder of millions of North American Indians, over 40, 50 thousand Palestinians murdered, over 20 some thousand of them kids and women. They never paid for it. When there was an attempt to bring them up on war crimes, America said you better not. Nobody holds this man accountable for the evil he’s doing on the earth. A fugitive can kill and commit crimes and get away with it; they’re on the run.

“A vagabond”: a person who wanders from place to place without a home, having no settled home. That’s why Lamech said, if someone kills me, they get it seventy times seven, you kill them worse. Blood always follows blood; blood shall pursue you.

“And I will put enmity between thee and the woman”: between Satan and the woman, “and between thy seed and her seed”: between Cain and Seth. Between Cain’s line and Seth’s line; Satan’s line, God’s line. That’s why she said God hath appointed me another seed; that’s the seed the Lord is talking about.

Abel was also of that seed, of course, but Cain killed him. The enmity was there; God prophesied Cain killing Abel. That’s why the Lord gave her another seed.

sense.text: “This is the book of the generations of Adam.” “Male and female created he them; and blessed them, and called their name Adam”: everybody was called Adam.

“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Stop: why is it saying that Adam begat a son in his own likeness and in his own image? It doesn’t say that about Abel.

Adam had that understanding from the creation, when God gave it to him, and for the righteous seed to come down it had to come through Seth. Seth came out righteous. Seth came out as the man that Adam once was before his fall. Adam went off, but Seth came out in the manner in which Adam was before his fall. Seth is the righteous.
“And he begat sons and daughters”. Adam had sons and daughters after this, but the main important one was Seth. The Lord said, I’m dealing with Seth here.
“And begat sons and daughters”: sons and daughters after Enos.

Mahalaleel begat Jared. That name Jared is the same name Cain’s line had: when Cain’s kids had Irad, that is Jared back then, and now you have Jared over here on the righteous line. Jared begat Enoch: there was a city built called Enoch. So what we have here is a righteous Enoch and a wicked Enoch, a righteous Jared and a wicked Jared. Two sides of the same coin.
“And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah”: the man that lived the longest on the earth, the one in the video with the sword and the fire.

“And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters”. There’s a bunch of sons and daughters out here, but the ones that are named are the most important ones.

“And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.” How did he take him? He took him up the same way he took up Elijah.

Remember, Cain had Enoch and built a city called Enoch in the land of Nod; that’s a wicked Enoch. Then Irad, then down the line Lamech, and Lamech had Jabal and Jubal and Tubal–cain. Keep that in mind.

precepts.why: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” You read these names earlier. They’re all listed in the same verse: son of Enos, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.

“By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death”: he should not see a regular death; it was a different kind of death. “And was not found”: not found, the same way Elijah was not found, “because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.” He pleased God and he walked with God, and he was translated.

“Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us. The Lord hath wrought great glory by them through his great power from the beginning”: from the very beginning, from Genesis. “Men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding, and declaring prophecies”. They “were the glory of their times.”

“There be of them, that have left a name behind them”, and “some there be, which have no memorial; who are perished, as though they had never been; and are become as though they had never been born; and their children after them.” That’s why Genesis 5 says he had sons and daughters but we don’t read about them; we read about the particular names, Mahalaleel, Jared, Enos. Those are important; they left a name behind them.

“But these were merciful men, whose righteousness hath not been forgotten. With their seed shall continually remain a good inheritance, and their children are within the covenant.” “Their seed standeth fast”: the seed of these particular men stay steadfast in the faith, in righteousness, “and their children for their sakes”: their children also remain steadfast based upon their fathers’ sakes. “Their seed shall remain for ever, and their glory shall not be blotted out”: the righteous men who had righteous children are going to be born again and have righteous kids again, over and over. “Their bodies are buried in peace”, because they’re dead, but they come back: “their name liveth for evermore.”

“Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance to all generations.” Did Enoch have kids? Yes. Was he righteous? Yes. So when Enoch comes back and has the seed, they will be within the covenant. Go back to verse 3: they were “declaring prophecies”. Their righteous seed will be righteous after them for their sakes: when they come back to their kids, since they’re righteous, they come right back the same way as their father was.

Remember it said they were declaring prophecies. “And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.”

That saying was passed on from generation to generation to generation, through all the tradition of the children of the righteous, who remain within the covenant, and the Lord reiterated it back to Moses, and Moses wrote it down for us to remember.

sense.text:
In an old inscription, the town Adana is explained by the Assyrian tables with the Shemite word Nadu. The Assyrians named this place Adana, Nadu. Half of an inscribed limestone tablet from the great temple of the sun in southern Babylonia, in the archaic writing of the oldest known period, mentions the town Adana or Nadu, which is Nod, Genesis 4:16. Nadu was a south Babylonian city. So the city Nimrod built in is the same place Cain resided in: Nadu is Nod, the land of Nod in which the city Enoch was built. Nod is southern Babylon, eastward of the garden of Eden.

“And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.” He resided in the land of Nod and built the city called Enoch, the wicked Enoch, after his son Enoch, the wicked son.

Enoch is the Akkadian Unuk, the place of settlement, the ancient name of Iraq. The city of Enoch built in the land of Nod is Babylon. And the wicked Irad is Eridu, the great port of the Babylonians. They deified Methusael, the Cainite descendant we read in Genesis 4, as the husband of the goddess, with a shrine in the forest of Eridu. So they identified this man as a god.

Bring it full circle: Cain was the king or ruler of Babylon in Genesis, and the white man is the ruler and king of Babylon now. The wicked ruled Babylon then, the wicked rule Babylon now. Nothing new under the sun.

Enoch is the same as Iraq that Nimrod built on top of. That’s why, when they built that tower, the Lord came there and stopped them and confounded the languages: they gained the same evil wisdom Cain gained in that same area. Their understanding was on another level, a technological level. Nimrod had understanding from his forefather: Cain went over there, and Nimrod went over there and did the same thing Cain did, built the city and gained the same wisdom from the same spirits over there. And what is Esau? The daughter of Babylon. Nothing new.

The same mindset they had then is the same mindset they have now: the same architecture, the same philosophy, the same worship.

“And Methuselah lived an hundred eighty and seven years, and begat Lamech”. Didn’t Cain’s side bring forth Lamech? Cain’s side brought forth Enoch, Irad, Lamech. Remember Lamech said if anyone kills me he’ll be avenged seventy and sevenfold. This is a different Lamech; this is Seth’s Lamech.

“And he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed.”

The Lamech of Cain brought forth a son that brought forth destruction and death: Tubal–cain. This Lamech brought forth a son of righteousness and purity and deliverance. See how it’s the whole opposite: Cain’s Lamech bore a son out of death, and the other Lamech bore a child that would spare life on the boat.
“And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” So Lamech begat Noah.

precepts.why: “Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance to all generations. Noah was found perfect and righteous”. Noah was found perfect: who said man can’t be perfect? Noah was found perfect, and righteous, keeping commandments. “In the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world; therefore was he left as a remnant unto the earth, when the flood came.”

sense.text: “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.” He shortened men’s years. His spirit won’t always do with us anymore, because man went off and started going into sin.

The sons of God, the righteous line, started going off. “There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that”: aside from that, “when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.”

So you had three sets of people: you had the wicked, you had the sons of God, and you had regular people, insignificant, just daughters of men. The sons of God dealt with them, and I’m sure the wicked as well, but here it says the daughters of men.

“Noah walked with God”, just like Enoch did. It goes back to the verse above where the Lord says my spirit shall not always strive with man. When the spirit of God dwells in you, you are walking with God. So when it says Noah walked with God, it means the Lord was literally dwelling with Noah.

“The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.” Who was ruling it? Cain was ruling; that’s why it was filled with violence. The sons of God were influenced and the daughters of men were influenced by the wicked. Nothing new; today same thing.

“For all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.” You don’t read about no one killing anybody until you read Cain’s line: I have slain a man to my wounding. You don’t read Seth’s line doing that; it was Cain’s line killing people.

“The earth is filled with violence through them”. The sons of God were not innocent; I’m not saying that. They were doing wicked and killing each other as well, the same way we do now, but not to the extent Cain’s line was spreading the evil and violence. The influence of that violence and murder was multiplied because of the wicked that were ruling.
“Make thee an ark of gopher wood”: so make an ark.
Noah builds the ark: “And Noah did according unto all that the Lord commanded him.”
“And Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was upon the earth.”

“Of clean beasts, and of beasts that are not clean”: he knew the difference between clean and unclean. Back then the Lord was around, so he knew what was clean and what was unclean, and this is before Moses.

“The same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.” He caused the water to come out from underneath and the water to come from the top, like tsunamis and so forth.

“And the Lord shut him in”: the Lord closed the door. You know what’s happening at this point: people screaming, let us in. The Lord said nope, I’ll close the door, I’ll do it; no one’s coming in here but y’all. That’s it, door closed.
“The waters increased, and bare up the ark, and it was lift up above the earth”, because the water was high.
“All the high hills, that were under the whole heaven, were covered”: all the mountains were covered. No one survived. When you run and hide, regardless, you’re under the water, you’re done.
“And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, both of fowl”: birds too. Wherever they fly, they all drowned; the water was too high.
Everything died.
“I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake”, “for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth”: men are born wicked. Man is prone to sin.

“While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.” He won’t flood the earth again. That’s why he made the rainbow, as a sign he won’t flood the earth again as he did before.
“And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.” Erech, where Nimrod was. Shinar is pretty much the land of Nod originally.
“And afterward were the families of the Canaanites spread abroad”: a bunch of children.

“These are the sons of Ham, after their families, after their tongues, in their countries, and in their nations.” It starts with the sons of Ham, and we end it right there regarding the sons of Ham, because we mentioned earlier the giants in the days of old.

Finishing Genesis 10 regarding Ham. We read earlier about the giants that were in those days; eventually the flood came and killed all of them as well. “The Kenites, and the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites, And the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Rephaims, And the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.” These are ten Hamitic nations.
Focus on the Rephaims in verse 20. Remember, Noah came, the flood came, and killed the daughters of men, killed the bulk of the sons of God, killed the wicked, killed the giants.

precepts.why:
They “came unto Hebron; where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of Anak, were.” “Now Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.” They cut down “a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bare it between two upon a staff”: the fruits were massive, huge.

They came back to Moses and Aaron and all the congregation and said, “surely it floweth with milk and honey; and this is the fruit of it. Nevertheless the people be strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled, and very great: and moreover we saw the children of Anak there.” They were doing surveillance, intel on the land.

Caleb said, “Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it. But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.” They brought up an evil report: “a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof”. They were scared, and they brought that fear back to the people. “All the people that we saw in it are men of a great stature. And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.”

The sons of Anak are the ones called the Rephaims in Genesis 15:20. They were huge; these were giants. Remember the giants of old all got killed, but when Noah had his three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, the same three sets of people that were before the flood came right back through those sons. Those giants came back through Ham.

“The Emims dwelt therein in times past, a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims; Which also were accounted giants, as the Anakims; but the Moabites call them Emims.” So they were called Anakims, the children of Anak, and the Moabites referred to them as Emims.

“The Horims also dwelt in Seir beforetime; but the children of Esau succeeded them, when they had destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead”. Esau took that land over from the Horites.

“That also was accounted a land of giants: giants dwelt therein in old time; and the Ammonites call them Zamzummims”. The giants were all given different names by different nations, but they were giants.

You had giants in the time of old when the sons of God were around, and you had giants in the time when the sons of God, the Israelites, were around. It’s the same thing all over again: the wicked, the righteous, everybody else, and giants.

“There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.” We read about those in the land of Canaan. “Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them: But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.”

The same giants, expert in war, like the ones Israel saw in the land. They were destroyed by the flood. Giants then, and in this particular time giants back again.

The Philistines were also of stature. All the giant nations came out of Ham. “The labour of Egypt, and merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans, men of stature”: Egypt, Ethiopia, the Sabeans, men of stature.

The Egyptians, who today would be the Nilotic Sudanese, the Ethiopians, the Somalians: they are all men of stature. That’s what we’re reading about: men of stature. The Egyptians were very tall, 7 feet, 8 feet, 9 feet tall.

sense.text: “Let us make brick, and burn them throughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter”: that is their technology.

“Let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.” They were trying to avoid getting flooded.

When Nimrod gained power on the earth they were building a tower, because that is what that power, that demonic authority, does: it builds a tower. It is the same allegory over and over. Every kingdom conquered adds a level to the tower of confusion. America is this tower, everyone gathered here together; Britain is this tower; Washington DC is this tower; New York is his tower; the capitals.

“The people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do: and now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do.” It means they would be successful in what they did: anything they could imagine, they were doing it. It’s the same mindset the white boy has today, that men have got today.

“Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.” So the Lord scattered them, and they left off building the city and that tower. “Therefore is the name of it called Babel.”

This is the land Nimrod built, where he tried to have all nations come together. That is what you would call the United States today: this is the ancient United States. Babylon is all nations coming together to go against and rebel against God. It’s Babylon all over again; it’s America all over again.
“These are the generations of Shem: Shem was an hundred years old, and begat Arphaxad two years after the flood.” From here the line of Shem is followed, generation by generation, down to Terah.
“Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran.” Terah begat Abram, who became our forefather Abraham.

precepts.why:
The same set of people that were around before the flood came back around in Israel’s time. Back then you had the wicked, you had the righteous, you had the daughters of men, and you had the giants, and they all got killed in the flood, except the sons of God who remained on the ark: Noah. Noah had three sons, and those sons replenished the same nations that were around back then. So far Ham brought back the giants, the giants of old that were expert in war and stupid.

“Sem and Seth were in great honour among men.” It is not a coincidence that Shem and Seth are in the same verse. Seth’s line got put to death in the flood, except through Noah, the survivor of the flood, and then comes Shem. Watch: “and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.” Shem, Seth and Adam were above every living thing in creation, and in great honour.

“Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” Out of Seth came Noah, Noah brought forth Shem, and out of Shem came forth all righteous men. That is why those two are named together in Ecclesiasticus 49:16.

“When they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, and had gotten them many children, and were a great people, they began again to be more ungodly than the first.” This happened in Genesis 4, then it happened in Noah’s time, then it happened again.

“Now when they lived so wickedly before thee, thou didst choose thee a man from among them, whose name was Abraham. Him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will.” Unto him only: nobody else, not all people, not all nations. Only to Abraham did the Most High show his will, “and madest an everlasting covenant with him, promising him that thou wouldest never forsake his seed.”

sense.text: “Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto the Lord.” Remember what happened with Cain: there was wickedness and murder. Then Adam brought forth Seth, Seth brought forth Enos, and then men began to call upon the name of the Lord. ‘Then’ means there was evil going on. We read in Ezra how evil spread all over again, and out of that evil came Abraham.

“There he builded an altar unto the Lord, and called upon the name of the Lord.” That is the same thing Enos did in Genesis 4: when wickedness was taking over, ruling and dominating, here come the righteous calling upon the name of the Lord once again.

It happens over and over and over again, the same thing today: evil takes over, and righteousness rises up and calls upon the name of the Lord.

This shows what that stone is and what that sword is. “Unto him thou gavest Isaac, and unto Isaac also thou gavest Jacob and Esau. As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee”: the Most High chose Jacob for himself, “and put by Esau”: I don’t want Esau, out of here. “And so Jacob became a great multitude”: that’s us.

The wicked had a deal with the devil: the more blood he sheds, the more power he gains. That is how Esau operates. Herod read Daniel, read Isaiah 63 and Isaiah 34, and understood them: if I kill this born King I can rule forever, but if he is born and grows up, he will teach those to rise against me. But he failed. No matter how much blood is shed, no matter how much demonic worship, body sacrifices and ceremonies, the good cannot be stopped. Christ is the born King first, and then the righteous seed under him; we are the born kings that must come.

precepts.why:
This sums up the balance: “Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” “So look upon all the works of the most High”, especially regarding man: “there are two and two, one against another.” Good is always against evil. That is ‘a law that cannot be transgressed’.

As evil takes over, righteousness has to show up to oppose it. There has to be a balance; evil cannot last forever. When evil takes over, good shows up. When Cain took over, Seth was born. When evil came again, Noah was born. When evil came again, Abraham was born. Esau takes over, and we’re born: we’re here. That is why saviours shall rise from mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau. That’s us. The evil is so bad on the earth, that’s what you see taking place today: the saviours are rising up.

Esau looks at all the evil he has done on this earth, and he is waiting for the righteous to stand up. That is how he knows his time is short: oh damn, these dudes are raising up, they’re getting up on their feet, they’re keeping the commandments. He knows his time is short by looking at us.

“All things are double one against another: and he hath made nothing imperfect.” Everything serves a purpose, whether it’s wicked or righteous. They were all made and serve their purpose, one against the other.

sense.text: “The children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus?” They were fighting in the womb, because they were going to be enemies in the womb and outside the womb.

“Two nations are in thy womb”: two different nations of people in your womb, “and two manner of people”: they look entirely different from each other, two behaviors, two different looks. They “shall be separated”, not joined; they will not get along.

“And the one people shall be stronger than the other people”: we’re stronger than them. “And the elder shall serve the younger”: they will serve us eventually, when Christ returns.
“His hand took hold on Esau’s heel.” Remember what we read earlier: it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. That is why Jacob grabbed that heel.

“And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed.” Thy seed is Satan’s seed, Cain, and Esau; her seed is Abel and Seth, and Jacob.

“It shall bruise thy head”: that goes into Adam first and foremost, but then it goes into Christ, of course. “And thou shalt bruise his heel”: your seed shall bruise his heel. That is why Jacob grabbed the heel. Her appointed seed would bruise his heel.

Genesis 3:15 is a summary of Daniel 2:32-34: the head bruised is Christ, and the heel is Esau’s empire, smitten by the stone.

precepts.why: This is the bruising of the head. “He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief”, and “we esteemed him not.” “But he was wounded for our transgressions”: Christ was wounded for our transgressions. “He was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.” With his death we received salvation. That covers the ‘bruise thy head’ part.

The evil spirit of the devil was in our own wicked people, the Pharisees, the Sadducees and the scribes, and they placed him into the hands of devils, Rome. Satan was involved in all of that: the evil spirit of our brothers who hated their brother, Christ, and placed him into the hands of the Romans, who were the children of Esau, or Cain again. That is the bruising of the head.

“Unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed”: the wicked of our people disallowed him, those who had the devil in them, whose father is the devil, as Christ said in John 8:44. In the movie King Arthur there is a sword in a stone. The stone is Christ, and only the chosen righteous line can pull that sword out of that stone. The wicked think that if they kill the Israelites, the Bible will answer only to them and they can teach whatever they want; but that’s not how it works. “The same is made the head of the corner”: bruise thy head.

“And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient: whereunto also they were appointed.” They were appointed to be rebellious against him and to have him bruised, based upon the prophecy of Genesis 3:15.

“The Lord hath also a controversy with Judah, and will punish Jacob according to his ways”: the context is Jacob. “He took his brother by the heel in the womb.” Jacob took his brother by the heel in the womb; they were fighting in the womb. Rebekah asked why this was happening: because they are going to be enemies in the womb and outside the womb. It is the battle between good and evil.

“And by his strength he had power with God”: power to wrestle God, an angel. That’s why his name was changed. That’s what Israel means: prince of the power of God.

Still on the heel: Satan will bruise your head, but your seed shall bruise his heel. “Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.” Why did his hand hold the heel of Esau, in the womb and outside the womb? “For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

That explains why Esau came out first, and it also explains why Ishmael came first: evil always comes first. Ishmael was made first and Isaac came after; Esau came out first and Jacob came after. That’s how it works.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand.” The hand of man is all the other nations. They are in between Jacob’s hand and Esau’s heel, the middlemen, the daughters of men. The main battle for world power and rulership is the sons of God versus the sons of the devil, and everybody else is in between the hand and the heel: the nations are NPCs, non-playable characters, the extras in the background of the movie.

We dealt with the head being bruised: that’s Christ, going into Adam as well. Now the heel. Daniel was shown the dream Nebuchadnezzar had regarding his kingdom and all the kingdoms to come later that were going to gain rulership on the earth, to whom Satan gave power.

“This image’s head was of fine gold, his breast and his arms of silver, his belly and his thighs of brass, his legs of iron”: strong metals. Then “his feet part of iron and part of clay.” When an image that big and tall has all those heavy metals on top and iron and clay feet, can it stand long? It will fall, because the foot is weak. And part of your foot is your heel.

“Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands.” Who is that stone? 1 Peter 2:7: Christ. It “smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.” Esau is the feet and the legs, and the stone comes and hits the heel. Thou shalt bruise his heel means your empire, your last, America and the European Union, will be destroyed. They are the children of the wicked.

“Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together”: all nations destroyed, from Ham all the way down to Edom, from Babylon all the way to Edom, who is new Babylon. They “became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors”, “that no place was found for them.” “And the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth”: and we rule the planet.

sense.text: “The indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies.” Their slain cast out, their stink coming up out of their carcases, the mountains melted with their blood, “and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: nuclear destruction, war.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven”: in this heaven on the earth here. “Behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” The people of his curse: what he said in Genesis 3:14 and 4:11, cursed shall you be above all cattle. That’s why your skin looks that way.

We are not the only ones who know this regarding Cain and Esau. A book called West African Studies says the African mind received white training; that happened to us, being taught inferiority and weakness. It tells the story Africans in touch with the Muhammadan tradition, which has the same Semitic source, the Bible and Ishmael, tell to account for the blackness and whiteness of men: when Cain killed Abel he was horrified at himself and terrified of God, carried the body about for years trying to hide it, until he saw a crow scratching a hole in the desert sand and buried it, ‘but his children were white’. ‘From Cain came the white races’, while Abel’s children, Seth’s children, are black, as all men were before the first murder.

So the nations know. Esau commits all kinds of evil and sin but frowns upon the dark nations as more deeply steeped in sin than himself. Traditionally the nations knew the white races came out of Cain, and the Bible says it.

“O virgin daughter of Babylon”: Psalms 137 shows that the daughter of Babylon is Edom. The attributes of Edom and Ham are so direct because they have a correlation with each other: they both deal with the same evil spirits. That’s why Esau borrows from Egypt and from Babylon: the dollar, the Egyptian eye of Ra, New Year’s, Christmas, which is Babylonian, the obelisks in Washington DC, in Rome, Italy, and in Central Park. They reverence Babylon because they are the daughter of Babylon.

“Come down, and sit in the dust”, “sit on the ground”, because what Nimrod failed to do, Esau succeeded in doing: gathering all nations together as one, democracy, all nations coming over here, the melting pot. Same thing: building a tower of confusion.

“There is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans”: no more kingdom for you, no more rulership. “For thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate”: people are going to see who you really are.
“I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man”: I’m going to show up here in my angelic power; I’m going to come here and destroy you personally.

“I was wroth with my people”: I was mad at my people at first. “I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand.” Esau, it wasn’t your doing; I put them into your hand. But you’re so prideful you think you did it by your own hands. “Thou didst shew them no mercy”: no mercy at all whatsoever; you broke us down to the smallest denominator, “upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke.”

“I shall be a lady for ever”: you said you’re going to rule forever. “So that thou didst not lay these things to thy heart”: you forgot that I gave you power to rule over my people. “Neither didst remember the latter end of it”: you forgot your judgment. You forgot what I told Cain.

“Thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am”: that says I’m God, “and none else beside me”: there’s no other nation on the earth that could rule better than me or beside me. “I shall not sit as a widow”: I will lose no loved ones, no allies. “Neither shall I know the loss of children”: I will lose no citizens.

“But these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood”: you lose your citizens and your allies. “For the multitude of thy sorceries”: the Masonic lodges, the sorceries, the evil blood sacrifices and ceremonies, the idolatry, all of that, “and for the great abundance of thine enchantments.”

“Thou hast said, None seeth me”: no one knows who I am, the daughter of Babylon. “Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me.” Ezekiel 28 says the same.

precepts.why:
“Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” That was the day the first temple was destroyed: the children of Edom said destroy it, destroy it, even to the foundation.

“O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed; happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us. Happy shall he be, that taketh and dasheth thy little ones against the stones.” It’s going to be a great day when that happens. He calls Edom the daughter of Babylon, so now we know who Isaiah 47:1 is speaking to regarding the daughter of Babylon: it is Edom.

sense.text:
“Say unto the prince of Tyrus”: this is talking about Edom. “Thou hast said, I am a God”, the same as Isaiah 47 said. “I sit in the seat of God”: people worship me. When they see God, when they see Christ, they see me; when they see the children of God, they see my people; when they go to seek and learn about God, they come to my churches, my chapels, my institutions. “In the midst of the seas”: in the midst of all nations; all nations follow behind what I say.

“Yet thou art a man, and not God, though thou set thine heart as the heart of God”: you feel you can do what God does, create man in your image, create woman in your image, create your doctrines and your philosophies, and people fall behind you.

“Thou art wiser than Daniel”: the left hand, the left side, the evil angel showed him things beyond Daniel. “There is no secret that they can hide from thee.” He knows who he is, and if he knows who he is, he knows who we are too. That’s why they convert to Judaism: they’re learning our customs, learning everything about us.

“Thou hast gotten thee riches, and hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures”: you gained wealth, like the man in the movie who conquered everyone and built his tower in gold. “And thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches.”

“I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations: and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom”: as Isaiah 47 said, you’re going to be in widowhood. “And they shall defile thy brightness”: that’s Lucifer. That goes back to Isaiah 14, O Lucifer, fallen from heaven. All this is talking about Tyrus, but it’s really talking about America.
“They shall bring thee down to the pit”: Isaiah 14 again.

“Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God?” Are you going to say you’re a god while you’re getting stabbed to death, killed, blown up and burnt alive, when them bombs hit America? “But thou shalt be a man, and no God, in the hand of him that slayeth thee.”
“Thou shalt die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers”: his own allies. That is talking about Esau. Now watch: he’s going to flip.
“Take up a lamentation upon the king of Tyrus”: the same context. “Thou sealest up the sum, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty”: you gained wisdom, wealth, power and perfection.

“Thou hast been in Eden the garden of God.” Was Esau ever in Eden? No. Who was in Eden? Cain was in Eden; the devil was in Eden. “Every precious stone was thy covering”: you had wealth, you were in paradise, surrounded by precious stones. All these materials are found in paradise.

“The workmanship of thy tabrets and of thy pipes was prepared in thee in the day that thou wast created.” Earlier we read that Cain’s descendant was a master of the harp and music. That skill was already placed in him before he was created, down the line.

“Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth.” What does he cover? He covers the identity of our people and the knowledge of our God. He is the cover, he is the confusion, the messenger of confusion. He whitewashes everything: he whitewashes the Messiah, the angels, God, the scriptures and the nations. He is the flaming sword going back and forth.

“And I have set thee so”: that is what he was born to do; you cannot change him. “Thou wast upon the holy mountain of God”: you were in the kingdom. “Thou hast walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire”: you were in paradise.
“Thou wast perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee.” You were good for a while, but it was a matter of time: that is your purpose.

“By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned.” He knows what he is doing is against God and he doesn’t care: he feels he is God, he has replaced God. “Therefore I will cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God”: I will take you out of power. “And I will destroy thee, O covering cherub”: O covering messenger, O covering demon, “from the midst of the stones of fire”, from the midst of your paradise.

“Thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness”: Lucifer once again. “I will cast thee to the ground”: Isaiah 14 again. “I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee”, and know that you are not a God but a man.

“Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries”: that’s his church system. “By the iniquity of thy traffick”: his trade, his business. “Therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee”: nuclear fire. “I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee”, and they will all know you’re not a God.
“Thou shalt be a terror, and never shalt thou be any more”: you’re going to be removed out of the earth, removed from existence.

precepts.why:
“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof.” The wicked covers the faces of the judges. Who are they? God, his Son, Israel, the angels. He covers them.

“If not, where, and who is he?” What other nation whitewashes images? None. It’s the wicked, Edom, that does that: the anointed cherub that covereth.

“For that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first”: Israel fell, goodness fell on the earth, and evil prevailed. “And that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition”: the son of hell.

“Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.” That is what we read in Tyrus, and in Isaiah 47 of the daughter of Babylon: the same thing.

“For the mystery of iniquity doth already work”: he was already ruling in Paul’s time as the Romans, and now as the Americans, because America is an extension of Rome. Russia, Spain, Britain and France are extensions of Rome: the same man with different titles. “Only he who now letteth will let”: only God lets him rule, “until he be taken out of the way”, when the time of the Gentiles is up.

“And then shall that Wicked be revealed”, when his time starts coming up, “whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth.” The spirit of his mouth is those in this room: we have the spirit of his mouth. “And shall destroy with the brightness of his coming”: that is Christ coming here and destroying him.

“Whose coming is after the working of Satan”: going back to Cain, the same thing, “with all power and signs and lying wonders”: power, technology, nuclear technology, the power of the sun.

sense.text: “Stand now with thine enchantments”: stand now in your witchcraft, “and with the multitude of thy sorceries”, your wicked elders and secret witches. “Wherein thou hast laboured from thy youth”: from his very beginning. “If so be thou mayest prevail”: let’s see if you win now.

“Thou art wearied in the multitude of thy counsels”: you’re getting weaker, falling apart by the day. “Let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators”: your sorcerers, your witches and your demonic counselors, “stand up, and save thee from these things that shall come upon thee.”
“Behold, they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them; they shall not deliver themselves from the power of the flame.”

precepts.why:
This ends it. “Thou shalt not be joined with them in burial, because thou hast destroyed thy land, and slain thy people: the seed of evildoers shall never be renowned.”

“Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers”: for the iniquity of Cain, the fugitive and vagabond. “That they do not rise”: Obama is going to be wrong in that day. “Nor possess the land”: nor possess our land, “nor fill the face of the world with cities.” The twelve tribes will.
